title: Research
text:
Grounded Multimodal Reasoning

CURRENT Ph.D. RESEARCH · ONGOING

How can an AI system understand what an object may enable in a new situation, rather than simply recalling its conventional category or familiar function?
My current research explores how intelligent systems form and refine grounded concepts from multimodal evidence and human interaction. I am particularly interested in object–action understanding: how AI systems interpret plausible interactions in complex and unfamiliar environments.
This work investigates broader questions about how perception, language, and interaction contribute to concept formation and generalization.
The research is conducted within ARCLIGHT, part of DARPA’s Environment-driven Conceptual Learning program, through a collaboration between Boston Fusion and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
Because this work is ongoing, this page focuses on its motivating questions and broader scientific context rather than unpublished implementation details.

title: Research
text:
Trustworthy Language Generation
Alongside my primary Ph.D. research, I collaborate on methods for identifying AI-generated language while balancing verifiability, robustness, and generation quality.
This research includes linguistically informed and probability-aware approaches to LLM watermarking, with an emphasis on reliable detection and broader public verifiability.
Selected outcomes include papers accepted to ACL 2026 and AAAI 2026.

title: Research
text:
Structured Knowledge and Retrieval
My earlier research examined how structured knowledge and multiple representations can improve information retrieval and recommendation.
This work includes knowledge hypergraphs for recommendation, contrastive representation learning, and entity retrieval methods that combine term matching, semantic similarity, and topic evidence.
